_meta.description: Great Feast variants for the Divine Liturgy: antiphons, troparia/kontakia, prokeimenon, alleluia, entrance hymn, megalynarion, communion hymn.
_meta._note: Extracted from server.js GREAT_FEAST_VARIANTS const (lines 1211-1670) to separate liturgical data from application logic. Keys are feast-key strings matched by getGreatFeastKey().
_meta.source: OCA Department of Liturgical Music and Translations service texts (Thee/Thy register)

circumcision._note: Circumcision of our Lord (Jan 1), cocelebrated with St. Basil the Great (whose Liturgy is served). Antiphons intentionally omitted so typical antiphons (Bless the Lord / Praise the Lord) render — Circumcision does not have its own festal antiphons in OCA typikon. Basil's cocelebrated troparion/kontakion/prokeimenon/alleluia/koinonikon come from cocelebrated-overlays.json '1-1' as .secondary. Discovered 2026-07-02 via judge sweep — the Circumcision feast propers were absent because 1-1 wasn't in the Great Feast key map.
circumcision.label: The Circumcision of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ

kontakia.text:
The Lord of all accepts to be circumcised,
thus, as He is good, excises the sins of mortal men.
Today He grants the world salvation,
while light-bearing Basil, hierarch of the Creator, rejoices in heaven,
as an initiate of Christ, the divine Light.

prokeimenon.refrain: O Lord, save Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance!
prokeimenon.verse: Unto Thee, O Lord, will I call, O my God, be not silent unto me.

verses: Give ear, O shepherd of Israel, Thou Who leadest Joseph like a flock!

circumcision.communionHymn: Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise Him in the highest! Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!
circumcision.entranceHymn: Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ. O Son of God, Who wast circumcised in the flesh for our sakes, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia.
circumcision.megalynarion: In thee rejoiceth, O full of grace, all creation, the ranks of Angels and the human race. O sanctified Temple and rational Paradise, boast of virgins, from whom God was incarnate and became a little Child — our God from before the ages! For He made thy womb a throne, and thy body more spacious than the heavens. In thee rejoiceth, O full of grace, all creation. Glory to thee.

nativity.label: The Nativity of Christ

first.refrain: Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us.
verses: I will give thanks unto the Lord with my whole heart, in the council of the upright and in the congregation.
Great are the works of the Lord, sought out according to all His desires.
His work is praise and majesty, and His righteousness endureth forever.
He hath made His wonderful works to be remembered; the Lord is gracious and full of compassion.
first.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

second.refrain: O Son of God, born of the Virgin, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
verses: Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord; in His commandments shall he greatly delight.
His seed shall be mighty upon the earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed.
Glory and riches shall be in his house, and his righteousness endureth forever.
Unto the upright there hath risen a light in the darkness; He is gracious, and compassionate, and righteous.
second.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

third.refrain: Thy Nativity, O Christ our God, has shone to the world the light of wisdom! For by it, those who worshipped the stars were taught by a Star to adore Thee, the Sun of Righteousness, and to know Thee, the Orient from on high. O Lord, glory to Thee!
verses: The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand, until I make Thine enemies Thy footstool.
The Lord shall send the rod of Thy strength out of Zion: rule Thou in the midst of Thine enemies.
With Thee is dominion in the day of Thy power, in the splendors of Thy saints.

troparia.rubric: Troparion of the Nativity of Christ, Tone 4:
troparia.text:
Thy Nativity, O Christ our God,
has shone to the world the Light of knowledge;
for by it, those who worshipped the stars
were taught by a star to adore Thee,
the Sun of Righteousness,
and to know Thee, the Dayspring from on High.
O Lord, glory to Thee!

kontakia.rubric: Kontakion of the Nativity of Christ, Tone 3:
kontakia.text:
Today the Virgin gives birth to the Transcendent One,
and the earth offers a cave to the Unapproachable One!
Angels with shepherds glorify Him.
The wise men journey with a star,
since for our sake the Pre-Eternal God was born as a young Child.

prokeimenon.refrain: All the earth shall worship Thee and shall sing to Thee; they shall sing to Thy Name, O Most High!
prokeimenon.verse: Make a joyful noise unto God, all the earth; sing of the glory of His Name; give glory to His praise.

verses: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands.
Day unto day pours forth speech, and night unto night declares knowledge.

nativity.entranceHymn: Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ. O Son of God, born of the Virgin, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
nativity.megalynarion: Magnify, O my soul, the most pure Virgin Theotokos, more honorable and more glorious than the heavenly hosts! I behold a strange and most glorious mystery: the cave a heaven, the Virgin a cherubic throne, and the manger a noble place in which Christ, the uncontained God, was laid. Let us sing and magnify Him!
nativity.communionHymn: The Lord has sent redemption to His people. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

theophany.label: The Baptism of Christ (Theophany)

first.refrain: Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us.
verses: When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of strange language,
Judah was His sanctuary, Israel His dominion.
The sea saw it and fled; Jordan was driven back.
What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? O Jordan, that thou wast driven back?
first.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

second.refrain: O Son of God, baptized in the Jordan, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
verses: I love the Lord because He has heard the voice of my supplication.
Because He inclined His ear to me, therefore I will call on Him as long as I live.
The snares of death encompassed me; the pangs of Sheol laid hold on me; I suffered distress and anguish, then I called on the Name of the Lord.
Gracious and righteous is the Lord; and our God is merciful.
second.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

third.refrain: When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest. For the voice of the Father bare witness to Thee, and called Thee His beloved Son; and the Spirit, in the form of a dove, confirmed the truthfulness of His word. O Christ our God, who hast revealed Thyself and hast enlightened the world, glory to Thee!
verses: O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good; for His mercy endureth forever.
Let the house of Israel now say that He is good, for His mercy endureth forever.
Let the house of Aaron now say that He is good, for His mercy endureth forever.
Let all that fear the Lord now say that He is good, for His mercy endureth forever.

troparia.text:
When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan,
the worship of the Trinity was made manifest;
for the voice of the Father bare witness to Thee,
and called Thee His beloved Son.
And the Spirit, in the form of a dove,
confirmed the truthfulness of His word.
O Christ our God, who hast revealed Thyself
and hast enlightened the world, glory to Thee!

kontakia.text:
Today Thou hast appeared to the world,
and Thy Light, O Lord, hath shone upon us,
who with understanding praise Thee:
"Thou hast come, Thou hast appeared,
O Light Unapproachable!"

prokeimenon.refrain: Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord. God is the Lord and has revealed Himself to us.
prokeimenon.verse: O give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures forever.

verses: Bring to the Lord, O ye sons of God, bring to the Lord young rams.
The voice of the Lord is upon the waters; the God of glory has thundered, the Lord, upon many waters.

theophany.entranceHymn: Blessed is He that cometh in the Name of the Lord. God is the Lord and hath revealed Himself to us. O Son of God, baptized in the Jordan, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
theophany.megalynarion: Magnify, O my soul, the most pure Virgin Theotokos, more honorable than the heavenly hosts! No tongue knows how to praise thee worthily, O Theotokos; even Angels are overcome with awe praising thee. But since thou art good, accept our faith; for thou knowest our love inspired by God! Thou art the defender of Christians, and we magnify thee.
theophany.communionHymn: The grace of God has appeared for the salvation of all men. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

meeting.label: The Meeting of the Lord (Presentation)

troparia.rubric: Troparion of the Meeting of the Lord, Tone 1:
troparia.text:
Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos, Full of Grace!
From thee shone the Sun of Righteousness, Christ our God,
enlightening those who sat in darkness.
Rejoice and be glad, O righteous Elder,
thou didst accept in thine arms the Redeemer of our souls,
Who grants us the Resurrection!

kontakia.rubric: Kontakion of the Meeting of the Lord, Tone 1:
kontakia.text:
By Thy Nativity Thou didst sanctify the Virgin's womb
and didst bless Simeon's hands, O Christ God.
Now Thou hast come and saved us through love.
Grant peace to all Orthodox Christians, O only Lover of Man!

prokeimenon.refrain: My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.
prokeimenon.verse: For He has regarded the low estate of His handmaiden; for behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed.

verses: Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace, O Master, according to Thy word.
A light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to Thy people Israel.

meeting.megalynarion: O Virgin Theotokos, hope of all Christians, protect, preserve, and save those who hope in thee! In the shadow and letter of the Law, let us the faithful discern a figure: every male child that opens the womb is holy to God. Therefore we magnify the firstborn Word of the Father Who has no beginning, the Son firstborn of a Mother who had not known man.
meeting.communionHymn: I will receive the cup of salvation and call on the Name of the Lord. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

transfiguration.label: The Transfiguration of Christ
transfiguration.dismissalIntroit: May Christ our true God, Who was transfigured in glory on Mount Tabor,
apostichaVerses: The heavens are Thine, the earth also is Thine; the world and all that is in it, Thou hast founded them!
Tabor and Hermon shall rejoice in Thy Name!
transfiguration._apostichaVersesSource: Ps. 88:12,13 as printed in the St. John of Damascus (Tyler) Transfiguration Vigil booklet, 2026-08-05. Vespers aposticha on a Great Feast takes proper verses; without these the assembler falls back to the ordinary Ps. 122 table. Indexed from the SECOND sticheron — the first carries no verse.
transfiguration._dismissalIntroitSource: Clause taken verbatim from the feast's own Litya idiomelon in Tone 2 ('Thou wast transfigured in glory on Mount Tabor, O Christ God'), following the sentence pattern already used for ascension. The other 11 Great Feasts still have no dismissalIntroit and fall back to the generic 'May Christ our true God,' — do not fill them in without a comparable source.

first.refrain: Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us.
verses: Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised, in the city of our God, in His holy mountain.
Beautiful in elevation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion.
God is known in her palaces as a refuge.
As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of Hosts.
first.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

second.refrain: O Son of God, transfigured on the mountain, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
verses: His foundation is in the holy mountains. The Lord loveth the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are spoken of thee, O City of God.
The Most High Himself shall establish her.
I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon among those that know Me.
second.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

third.refrain: Thou wast transfigured on the mountain, O Christ God, revealing Thy glory to Thy disciples as far as they could bear it. Let Thine everlasting light also shine upon us sinners, through the prayers of the Theotokos! O Giver of Light, glory to Thee!
verses: The heavens are Thine, the earth also is Thine; the world and the fulness thereof, Thou hast founded them.
Tabor and Hermon shall rejoice in Thy name.
Blessed are the people who know the joyful sound.

troparia.text:
Thou wast transfigured on the mountain, O Christ God,
revealing Thy glory to Thy Disciples as far as they could bear it.
Let Thine everlasting Light also shine upon us sinners,
through the prayers of the Theotokos!
O Giver of Light, glory to Thee!

kontakia.text:
On the mountain Thou wast transfigured, O Christ God,
and Thy Disciples beheld Thy glory as far as they could see it;
so that when they would behold Thee crucified,
they would understand that Thy suffering was voluntary,
and would proclaim to the world
that Thou art truly the Radiance of the Father!

prokeimenon.refrain: O Lord, how manifold are Thy works! In wisdom hast Thou made them all.
prokeimenon.verse: Bless the Lord, O my soul! O Lord my God, Thou art very great!

verses: Thine are the heavens, and Thine is the earth.
Blessed are the people who know the joyful sound.

transfiguration.entranceHymn: Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ. O Son of God, transfigured on the mountain, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
transfiguration.megalynarion: Magnify, O my soul, the Lord Who was transfigured on Mount Tabor! Thy childbearing was without corruption; God came forth from thy body clothed in flesh, and appeared on earth and dwelt among men. Therefore we all magnify thee, O Theotokos!
transfiguration.communionHymn: O Lord, we will walk in the light of Thy countenance, and will exult in Thy name forever. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

sjd-mission-mountain._provenance: Transcribed from the 'St. John of Damascus Mission' antiphon sheets in the parish Transfiguration Liturgy booklet, 2026-08-06 (Common Chant). A mountain-themed psalm selection differing from the OCA DLMT set in `antiphons`. Stored in the file's Thee/Thy register; parishes on the modern register get You/Your via the pronoun transform, which is how the booklet prints Antiphon 3. Selected per-parish via rubrics_extra_json.antiphonSet — NOT the default.

first.refrain: Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us.
verses: Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth; sing of His name, give glory to His praise.
The voice of Thy thunder was in the whirlwind, Thy lightning lighted up the world, and the earth trembled.
Thou art clothed with honor and majesty, Who coverest Thyself with light as with a garment.
first.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

second.refrain: O Son of God, transfigured on the mountain, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
verses: Mount Zion in the far north is the city of the great King.
And He brought them to the mountain of His sanctuary, this mountain which His right hand had won.
The Mount Zion which He loved, He built as His sanctuary with mighty strength.
second.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

third.refrain: Thou wast transfigured on the mountain, O Christ God, revealing Thy glory to Thy disciples as far as they could bear it. Let Thine everlasting light also shine upon us sinners, through the prayers of the Theotokos! O Giver of Light, glory to Thee!
verses: Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved, but abideth forever.
As the mountains are round about Him, so the Lord is round about His people, from this time forth and forevermore.
Lord, who shall sojourn in Thy tent? Who shall dwell on Thy holy hill?
Who shall ascend the hill of the Lord? And who shall stand in His holy place?

transfiguration.entranceVerse: Send out Thy light and Thy truth; let them lead me, let them bring me to Thy holy mountain!
transfiguration._entranceVerseSource: Ps. 42:3, the proper eisodikon printed as 'Introit of the Little Entrance' in the parish Transfiguration Liturgy booklet, 2026-08-06. On a Great Feast of the Lord this replaces the ordinary 'Come, let us worship'.

postAmbonRite.label: Blessing of Grapes and Fruit
postAmbonRite.rubric: Immediately after the Prayer behind the Ambon, according to ancient custom, we observe the blessing of grapes as well as apples and other fruit. The fruit is censed as we sing:

prayers.incipit: Bless, O Lord, this new fruit of the vine…
prayers.citation: Prayer at the Partaking of Grapes — Festal Menaion p. 502; Great Book of Needs vol. 2 p. 352
Prayer for Them That Offer First Fruits — Great Book of Needs vol. 2 p. 353

postAmbonRite.sprinklingRubric: The priest sprinkles the grapes and fruit with holy water, saying (thrice):
postAmbonRite.sprinkling: These grapes and fruit are blessed and sanctified by the sprinkling of this holy water, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
postAmbonRite._source: Transcribed from the St. John of Damascus (Tyler) Transfiguration Liturgy booklet, 2026-08-06. The two priestly prayers are given there by incipit + book citation only, so they are rendered as cited rubrics rather than reconstructed. The rite ends by flowing into the usual 'Blessed be the name of the Lord' (thrice), which the Liturgy already emits.

elevation.label: The Elevation of the Cross

first.refrain: Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us.
verses: My God, my God, why hast Thou forsaken me? Why art Thou so far from helping me?
O my God, I cry in the daytime, but Thou hearest not; and in the night season.
But Thou art holy, O Thou that inhabitest the praises of Israel.
Our fathers trusted in Thee; they trusted, and Thou didst deliver them.
first.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

second.refrain: O Son of God, crucified in the flesh, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
verses: O God, why hast Thou cast us off forever? Why doth Thine anger smoke against the sheep of Thy pasture?
Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased of old.
Remember Mount Zion, wherein Thou hast dwelt.
God is our King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.
second.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

third.refrain: O Lord, save Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance! Grant victories to the Orthodox Christians over their adversaries, and by virtue of Thy Cross, preserve Thy habitation!
verses: O make a joyful noise unto the Lord, all ye lands; serve the Lord with gladness.
Come before His presence with singing; know ye that the Lord, He is God.
It is He that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are His people and the sheep of His pasture.

troparia.rubric: Troparion of the Elevation of the Cross, Tone 1:
troparia.text:
O Lord, save Thy people,
and bless Thine inheritance!
Grant victories to the Orthodox Christians
over their adversaries;
and by virtue of Thy Cross,
preserve Thy habitation!

kontakia.rubric: Kontakion of the Elevation of the Cross, Tone 4:
kontakia.text:
As Thou wast voluntarily raised upon the Cross for our sake,
grant mercy to those who are called by Thy Name, O Christ God;
make all Orthodox Christians glad by Thy power,
granting them victories over their adversaries
by bestowing on them the invincible trophy, Thy weapon of peace!

prokeimenon.refrain: Exalt the Lord our God; worship at His footstool, for He is holy!
prokeimenon.verse: The Lord reigns; let the peoples tremble.

verses: Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast gotten of old.
God is our King before the ages; He has worked salvation in the midst of the earth.

elevation.entranceHymn: Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ. O Son of God, crucified in the flesh, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
elevation.megalynarion: Magnify, O my soul, the most precious Cross of the Lord! Thou art a mystical Paradise, O Theotokos, who, though untilled, hast brought forth Christ; through Him the life-bearing wood of the Cross was planted on earth. Now at its Exaltation, as we bow in worship before it, we magnify thee!
elevation.communionHymn: The light of Thy countenance, O Lord, has been signed upon us. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

palmSunday.label: The Entry of the Lord into Jerusalem

first.refrain: Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!
verses: I love the Lord because He has heard the voice of my supplication.
Because He inclined His ear to me, therefore I will call on Him as long as I live.
The snares of death encompassed me; the pangs of hell laid hold on me.
I suffered distress and anguish, then I called on the Name of the Lord.
I will walk in the presence of the Lord in the land of the living.
first.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

second.refrain: O Son of God, seated on the colt of an ass, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
verses: I kept my faith, even when I said, "I am greatly afflicted."
What shall I render to the Lord for all the things He has given me?
I will receive the cup of salvation, and call upon the Name of the Lord.
I will pay my vows to the Lord in the presence of all His people.
second.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

third.refrain: By raising Lazarus from the dead before Thy Passion, Thou didst confirm the universal resurrection, O Christ God. Like the children with the palms of victory, we cry out to Thee, O Vanquisher of Death: "Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord."
verses: O give thanks to the Lord, for He is good; for His mercy endures forever.
Let the house of Israel say that He is good; for His mercy endures forever.
Let the house of Aaron say that He is good; for His mercy endures forever.
Let those who fear the Lord say that He is good; for His mercy endures forever.

troparia.rubric: Troparion of Entry of Our Lord into Jerusalem (Palm Sunday), Tone 1:
troparia.text:
By raising Lazarus from the dead before Thy Passion,
Thou didst confirm the universal resurrection, O Christ God.
Like the children with the palms of victory,
we cry out to Thee, O Vanquisher of Death:
"Hosanna in the highest!
Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord."

troparia.rubric: Troparion of Entry of Our Lord into Jerusalem (Palm Sunday), Tone 4:
troparia.text:
When we were buried with Thee in baptism, O Christ God,
we were made worthy of eternal life by Thy Resurrection.
Now we praise Thee and sing:
"Hosanna in the highest!
Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord!"

kontakia.rubric: Kontakion of Entry of Our Lord into Jerusalem (Palm Sunday), Tone 6:
kontakia.text:
Sitting on Thy throne in Heaven,
carried on a foal on earth, O Christ God,
accept the praise of angels and the songs of children, who sing:
"Blessed is He Who comes to recall Adam!"

prokeimenon.refrain: Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord. God is the Lord and has revealed Himself to us.
prokeimenon.verse: O give thanks to the Lord, for He is good; for His mercy endures forever.

verses: O sing to the Lord a new song, for He has done marvelous things!
All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.

palmSunday.entranceHymn: Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord. We bless thee from the house of the Lord. God is the Lord and He has revealed Himself to us.
palmSunday.megalynarion: God is the Lord and has revealed Himself to us! Celebrate the feast and come with gladness! Let us magnify Christ with palms and branches, singing: "Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord, our Savior!"
palmSunday.communionHymn: Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord. God is the Lord and has revealed Himself to us. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

ascension.label: The Ascension of the Lord

first.refrain: Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!
verses: Clap your hands, all peoples; shout to God with loud songs of joy!
For the Lord, the Most High is terrible; a great God over all the earth.
He subdued peoples under us, and nations under our feet.
God has gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet!
first.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

second.refrain: O Son of God, who ascended in glory, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
verses: Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised in the city of our God.
Mount Zion in the far north is the city of the great King.
Within her citadels God is known when He defends her.
For lo, the kings assembled; they came on together.
second.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

third.refrain: Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God, granting joy to Thy disciples by the promise of the Holy Spirit. Through the blessing they were assured that Thou art the Son of God, the Redeemer of the world.
verses: Hear this, all peoples; give ear, all inhabitants of the world.
Earth-born and the sons of men, rich and poor together.
My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be understanding.
I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will solve my riddle in psalmody.

troparia.text:
Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God,
granting joy to Thy Disciples by the promise of the Holy Spirit.
Through the blessing, they were assured
that Thou art the Son of God,
the Redeemer of the world!

kontakia.text:
When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sake,
and united earth to heaven,
Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God,
not being parted from those who love Thee,
but remaining with them and crying:
"I am with you, and there is no one against you!"

prokeimenon.refrain: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; and Your glory be over all the earth!
prokeimenon.verse: My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make melody.

verses: God has gone up with a shout; the Lord with the sound of a trumpet!
Oh, clap your hands, all you peoples. Shout to God with loud songs of joy!

ascension.entranceHymn: God has gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet. O Son of God, who ascended in glory, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
ascension.megalynarion: Magnify, O my soul, Christ the Giver of Life, Who hath ascended from earth to heaven! We the faithful, with one accord, magnify thee, the Mother of God, who, beyond reason and understanding, ineffably gave birth in time to the Timeless One.
ascension.communionHymn: God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!
ascension.dismissalIntroit: May Christ our true God, Who ascended in glory from us into heaven, and is seated at the right hand of God the Father,

dismissalTheotokos.priestCue: Magnify, O my soul, Christ the Giver of Life Who hath ascended from earth to heaven.
dismissalTheotokos.hymn: We the faithful, with one accord, magnify thee, the Mother of God, who, beyond reason and understanding, ineffably gave birth in time to the Timeless One.

pentecost.label: The Descent of the Holy Spirit (Pentecost)

first.refrain: Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!
verses: The heavens are telling the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims His handiwork.
Day to day pours forth speech, and night to night declares knowledge.
Their proclamation has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the universe.
first.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

second.refrain: O Gracious Comforter, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
verses: The Lord answer thee in the day of trouble! The Name of the God of Jacob protect thee!
May He send thee help from the sanctuary, and give thee support from Zion.
May He remember all thine offerings, and fulfill all thy plans.
second.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

third.refrain: Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God, who hast revealed the fishermen as most wise by sending down upon them the Holy Spirit; through them Thou didst draw the world into Thy net. O Lover of Man, glory to Thee!
verses: In Thy strength the king rejoices, O Lord, and exults greatly in Thy salvation.
Thou hast given him his heart's desire, and hast not withheld the request of his lips.
For Thou dost meet him with goodly blessings; Thou dost set a crown of fine gold upon his head.

troparia.text:
Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God,
who hast revealed the fishermen as most wise
by sending down upon them the Holy Spirit;
through them Thou didst draw the world into Thy net.
O Lover of Man, glory to Thee!

kontakia.text:
When the Most High came down and confused the tongues,
He divided the nations;
but when He distributed the tongues of fire,
He called all to unity.
Therefore, with one voice, we glorify the All-holy Spirit!

prokeimenon.refrain: Their proclamation has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the universe.
prokeimenon.verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands.

verses: By the Word of the Lord were the heavens made, and all the host of them by the Spirit of His mouth.
The Lord looked down from heaven; He saw all the sons of men.

pentecost.entranceHymn: Be exalted, O Lord, in Thy strength! We will sing and praise Thy power. O Gracious Comforter, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
pentecost.megalynarion: Rejoice, O Queen, glory of mothers and virgins! For no tongue, be it ever so gifted, hath power to praise thee worthily. Every mind is dizzied in attempting to comprehend thy childbearing. Wherefore, with one accord, we glorify thee!
pentecost.communionHymn: Let Thy good Spirit lead me on a level path. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

nativityTheotokos.label: The Nativity of the Theotokos

troparia.rubric: Troparion of the Nativity of the Theotokos, Tone 4:
troparia.text:
Thy nativity, O Virgin,
has proclaimed joy to the whole universe!
The Sun of righteousness, Christ our God,
has shone from thee, O Theotokos.
By annulling the curse,
He bestowed a blessing.
By destroying death, He has granted us eternal life.

kontakia.rubric: Kontakion of the Nativity of the Theotokos, Tone 4:
kontakia.text:
By thy nativity, O most pure Virgin,
Joachim and Anna are freed from barrenness;
Adam and Eve, from the corruption of death.
And we, thy people, freed from the guilt of sin, celebrate and sing to thee:
"The barren woman gives birth to the Theotokos, the nourisher of our Life."

prokeimenon.refrain: My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.
prokeimenon.verse: For He has regarded the low estate of His handmaiden; for behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed.

verses: Hear, O daughter, and consider and incline your ear.
The rich among the people shall entreat your favor.

nativityTheotokos.megalynarion: Magnify, O my soul, the most glorious birth of the Mother of God! Virginity is foreign to mothers; childbearing is strange for virgins. But in thee, O Theotokos, both were accomplished. For this all the earthly nations unceasingly magnify thee.
nativityTheotokos.communionHymn: I will receive the cup of salvation and call on the Name of the Lord. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

entryTheotokos.label: The Entry of the Theotokos into the Temple

troparia.rubric: Troparion of the Entry of the Theotokos, Tone 4:
troparia.text:
Today is the prelude of the good will of God,
of the preaching of the salvation of mankind.
The Virgin appears in the temple of God,
in anticipation proclaiming Christ to all.
Let us rejoice
and sing to her:
"Rejoice, O Fulfillment of the Creator's dispensation."

kontakia.rubric: Kontakion of the Entry of the Theotokos, Tone 4:
kontakia.text:
The most pure Temple of the Savior;
the precious Chamber and Virgin;
the sacred Treasure of the glory of God,
is presented today to the house of the Lord.
She brings with her the grace of the Spirit,
therefore, the angels of God praise her:
"Truly this woman is the abode of heaven."

prokeimenon.refrain: My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.
prokeimenon.verse: For He has regarded the low estate of His handmaiden; for behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed.

verses: Hear, O daughter, and consider and incline your ear.
The rich among the people shall entreat your favor.

entryTheotokos.megalynarion: The angels beheld the entrance of the Pure One and were amazed. How has the Virgin entered into the Holy of Holies? Since she is a living Ark of God, let no profane hand touch the Theotokos. But let the lips of believers unceasingly sing to her, praising her in joy with the angel's song: Truly, thou art more exalted than all, O pure Virgin!
entryTheotokos.communionHymn: I will receive the cup of salvation and call on the Name of the Lord. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

annunciation.label: The Annunciation

troparia.text:
Today is the beginning of our salvation,
the revelation of the eternal mystery!
The Son of God becomes the Son of the Virgin
as Gabriel announces the coming of Grace.
Together with him let us cry to the Theotokos:
Rejoice, O Full of Grace,
the Lord is with thee!

kontakia.text:
O Victorious Leader of Triumphant Hosts!
We, thy servants, delivered from evil, sing our grateful thanks to thee, O Theotokos!
As thou dost possess invincible might, set us free from every calamity
so that we may sing: Rejoice, O unwedded Bride!

prokeimenon.refrain: From day to day proclaim the salvation of our God!
prokeimenon.verse: Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth!

verses: He descends like rain upon the fleece, like raindrops that water the earth.
May His Name be blessed forever; may His Name continue as long as the sun!

annunciation.megalynarion: O earth, announce good tidings of great joy: O heavens, praise the glory of God! Since she is a living Ark of God, let no profane hand touch the Theotokos. But let the lips of believers unceasingly sing to her, praising her in joy with the angel's song: Rejoice, O Lady, full of grace, the Lord is with thee!
annunciation.communionHymn: The Lord has chosen Zion; He has desired it for His habitation. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

dormition.label: The Dormition of the Theotokos

troparia.text:
In giving birth thou didst preserve thy virginity.
In falling asleep thou didst not forsake the world, O Theotokos.
Thou wast translated to life, O Mother of Life,
and by thy prayers thou dost deliver our souls from death.

kontakia.text:
Neither the tomb, nor death had power over the Theotokos,
who is unsleeping in her intercessions and an unchanging hope in her protection.
For as the Mother of Life,
she was translated into life by Him who dwelt in her ever-virginal womb.

prokeimenon.refrain: My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.
prokeimenon.verse: For He has regarded the low estate of His handmaiden; for behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed.

verses: Arise, O Lord, into Thy resting place, Thou and the Ark of Thy holiness.
The Lord has sworn in truth to David, and He will not annul it.

dormition.megalynarion: The Angels, as they looked upon the Dormition of the Virgin, were struck with wonder, seeing how the Virgin went up from earth to heaven. The limits of nature are overcome in thee, O Pure Virgin: for birthgiving remains virginal, and life is united to death; a virgin after childbearing and alive after death, thou dost ever save thine inheritance, O Theotokos.
dormition.communionHymn: I will receive the cup of salvation and call on the Name of the Lord. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

pascha.label: The Holy Pascha — Resurrection of Christ

first.refrain: Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us.
verses: Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth! Sing the glory of His name; make His praise glorious!
Say to God: How awesome are Thy deeds! So great is Thy power that Thine enemies cringe before Thee.
Let all the earth worship Thee and praise Thee; let it praise Thy name, O Most High!
first.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

second.refrain: O Son of God, risen from the dead, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
verses: God be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause His face to shine upon us.
That Thy way may be known upon earth, Thy saving health among all nations.
Let the people praise Thee, O God; let all the people praise Thee.
second.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

third.refrain: Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!
verses: Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered; let them also that hate Him flee before Him.
As smoke is driven away, so drive them away; as wax melteth before the fire.
So let the wicked perish at the presence of God. But let the righteous be glad.

troparia.text:
Christ is risen from the dead,
trampling down death by death,
and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!

kontakia.text:
Thou didst descend into the tomb, O Immortal,
Thou didst destroy the power of death.
In victory didst Thou arise, O Christ God,
proclaiming, "Rejoice!" to the Myrrhbearing Women,
granting peace to Thine Apostles, and bestowing Resurrection on the fallen.

prokeimenon.refrain: This is the day which the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it!
prokeimenon.verse: O give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures forever.

verses: Thou, O Lord, shalt arise and have compassion on Zion.
The Lord looked down from heaven to the earth.

pascha.entranceHymn: In the gathering places bless ye God the Lord, from the wellsprings of Israel! O Son of God, risen from the dead, save us who sing to Thee: Alleluia!
pascha.megalynarion: The Angel cried to the Lady full of grace: Rejoice, O pure Virgin! Again I say: Rejoice! Thy Son is risen from His three days in the tomb! With Himself He has raised all the dead! Rejoice, all ye people! Shine! Shine! O new Jerusalem! The glory of the Lord has shone on thee! Exult now and be glad, O Zion! Be radiant, O pure Theotokos, in the Resurrection of thy Son!
pascha.communionHymn: Receive ye the Body of Christ; taste ye the Fountain of immortality. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!
